title: Modular Integrated AI Infrastructure (MiAI): From Deployment Modularity to Lifecycle Modularity
content: Artificial-intelligence infrastructure increasingly uses prefabricated modules, yet deployment boundaries need not match the different renewal clocks of computing and supporting assets. Here we introduce Modular Integrated AI Infrastructure (MiAI), a paradigm that co-designs physical assemblies, functional interfaces and renewal boundaries across computing, power, cooling, energy storage, communication and sensing-and-control. Drawing on modular integrated construction (MiC), multi-trade integrated mechanical, electrical and plumbing (MiMEP), and prefabricated modular data centres, MiAI combines factory integration and testing, transportable assemblies and standardized, reversible physical--digital connections to support staged deployment, selective renewal, relocation and multi-cycle reuse. It is physically modular, functionally integrated and temporally decoupled. We demonstrate its lifecycle-renewal mechanism through a differential lifecycle global-warming potential framework for compute transitions and exposed support infrastructure. Service-weighted effective retention, $R_{\mathrm{eff}}=q\Delta r v$, combines transition-exposed support scope, additional physical retention relative to a deployment-oriented modular baseline that already retains support assets, and qualified remaining service. Favourable outcomes arise above the burden threshold, $R_{\mathrm{eff}}>R_{\mathrm{eff}}^*$, so that retained-service credits exceed interface and transition burdens. In an illustrative normalized same-site configuration, the additional physical-retention threshold within the transition-exposed subset is $\Delta r^*=0.20$. Combining this break-even condition with physical retention limits separates favourable, burden-dominated and physically infeasible configurations. MiAI makes the renewal boundary an explicit design object, extending modularity from how AI infrastructure is delivered to what it preserves across technology generations.
